question: Is the rainfall-associated higher-order within-taxon spatial coherence broadly distributed across frog taxa, or dominated by one/few species?
response_per_species: For each pair and route-new species with k occupied wet stops, higher_order_mass = choose(max(k-1,0),2); otherwise 0.
decomposition: Because the matched rainfall coefficient is linear, the total higher-order coefficient equals the sum of species-specific coefficients using the same residualized design.

diagnostics.positive_share: Each positive species beta divided by the sum of positive species betas.
diagnostics.top1_top5: Largest and five-largest positive contribution shares.
diagnostics.hhi: Herfindahl index of positive contribution shares.
diagnostics.leave_one_species_out: Subtract each species beta from the total higher-order beta and report the minimum remaining beta.
diagnostics.contributing_taxa: Count species with positive beta and positive beta >=1% of total positive mass.

prefixed_rule.diffuse: top1 <=0.25 AND top5 <=0.60 AND HHI <=0.10 AND all leave-one-species-out total betas remain >0
prefixed_rule.threshold_source: Exactly reused from NAAMP_ROUTE_NEW_SPECIES_CONCENTRATION_CONTRACT_V0_1; no new cutoffs selected after higher-order endpoint readback.

interpretation: Diffuse support means no single taxon or small set of taxa is required for the higher-order rainfall coefficient.
It does not imply every species responds positively or that all taxa share one mechanism.
